summary.headline: Q2 FY27 standalone revenue rose 32.5% YoY to Rs 33.98 crore and PAT 41.2% to Rs 4.45 crore; order backlog Rs 39 crore.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue from operations was Rs 33.98 crore, up 25.1% QoQ and 32.5% YoY, with adjusted operational EBITDA of Rs 5.66 crore (16.6% margin, slightly below 17% a year earlier). PAT rose 41.2% YoY to Rs 4.45 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was Rs 61.14 crore (up 31.1%) and H1 PAT Rs 7.59 crore (up 55.2%). Management said the constraint has shifted from demand to plant throughput, and the Odisha SiC epitaxy facility is awaiting Odisha state statutory clearances before commercial production.

financial_highlights.change: +32.5% YoY vs Rs 25.64 crore; +25.1% QoQ vs Rs 27.16 crore
+41.2% YoY vs Rs 3.15 crore; PAT margin 12.5% vs 11.97%
+42.8% YoY vs Rs 7.25 crore; margin 16.9% vs 15.5%

financial_highlights.value: Rs 39 crore (also cited as Rs 17.4 crore in prepared remarks)
financial_highlights.change: Prepared remarks cite backlog up 38.9% from 31 March 2026 to Rs 17.4 crore; Q&A cites about Rs 39 crore

segments.name: High-power devices (HPD)
segments.commentary: Full in-house chain from wafer processing and diffusion to fabrication and product; certain bottleneck operations at about 90% utilisation, which management says can be doubled by adding machines. Silicon-based products reach up to 9000 V and 6000 A.

segments.name: Low-power devices (LPD) and equipment
segments.commentary: Mainly assembly-driven; management sees no capacity constraint, adding assembly benches and people as needed.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Management expects railway business to grow 70-80% YoY in quantity and value this year, with repeat orders received for existing and new products.

segments.name: Defence and export
segments.commentary: Defence prototype testing complete with first rail/defence orders awaited; first export order about 70% executed, with US market testing to follow.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward-looking revenue or EBITDA figures for the company or the Odisha plan, saying it prefers to avoid forward-looking statements, while saying it expects to do better than the current run-rate.

Odisha SiC epitaxy: commercial production depends on Odisha statutory, building and fire clearances, with no firm timeline; chairman hoped for this quarter (Q3), and management said November or at latest December 2026.
Epitaxy revenue estimate of Rs 12-15 crore over the next four to six months, per CFO Ankit Shah, covering the balance of the financial year; per-wafer realisation not given.

Chairman said SiC epi revenue would start within about three months; packaging (phase 1B) would take about 8-9 months (management also cited 9-12 months) to build once the bank term loan is sanctioned.
Base quarter: management said Q2 revenue of about Rs 34 crore should be the base, with no one-time revenue, and backlog of about Rs 39 crore gives scope to grow.
Railways expected to grow 70-80% YoY in quantity and value this year; defence first rail/defence orders awaited; first export order about 70% executed.

Chairman expects a ramp rather than a sharp jump, with no inflection date given; management said the Odisha project numbers would differ after FY29 or FY30, and the $100 million figure cited by an analyst was described as a revenue aspiration rather than a target market.
capex_capacity: Odisha SiC facility: clean room, 33 kV power infrastructure and SiC epitaxial reactors installed; commercial production awaits Odisha building and fire clearances, with management hoping for November, or at latest December 2026, and no firm timeline given.
Expected epitaxy revenue of Rs 12-15 crore over the next four to six months, per CFO; management expects about 90% of capacity covered by letters of intent.
Packaging (phase 1B) funded by term loan with about 5% government interest subsidy; bank has internal approvals and sanction letter is pending; packaging build estimated at 9-12 months once funded.
Management is installing two reactors initially and may need about five reactors soon; fabrication (phase 2) is a greenfield project with no timeline given.
demand_pricing: Order backlog at end Q2 is about Rs 39 crore per Q&A; management says demand is no longer the constraint and the problem has shifted to manufacturing throughput.
Management says SiC epi has specifications from international customers and letters of intent covering about 90% of initial capacity, though LOIs are non-binding.
Company plans to submit a development plan within about a month for indigenous BSV HVDC systems; tender sample supply 18 months and product supply 36 months.

Competition: management says the medium and high-power device segment has only four or five global competitors (ABB, Siemens, Hitachi, Toshiba) and no Indian rival; big new entrants focus on the last ~5% of the value chain (packaging, testing).

qa_highlights.question: When will the Odisha epitaxy plant be operational?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said almost everything is done and only internal reactor testing remains; start depends on Odisha building and fire clearances, with no firm timeline, though the chairman hoped for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 Rs 34 crore revenue a base run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it should be the base quarter, with no one-time revenue, and backlog offers scope to grow beyond it; no forward-looking numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: How is packaging (phase 1B) being funded and when does it start?
qa_highlights.answer: Term loan at closing stage; secured by promoters' immovable properties and FDs; bank has internal approvals, with a 5% government interest subsidy. No further equity planned for 1B, while 1A was fully equity funded.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue is expected from SiC epitaxy?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO estimated Rs 12-15 crore over the next four to six months from epitaxy; per-wafer realisation not given as pricing depends on thickness and specs.

qa_highlights.question: What are existing capacity and utilisation levels?
qa_highlights.answer: HPD bottleneck operations at about 90%, doubled by adding machines; LPD and equipment are assembly-limited with no capacity constraint.

risks_watch: Odisha statutory and building/fire clearances remain outstanding and have already delayed the epitaxy start beyond earlier expectations.
Bank sanction for the phase 1B packaging term loan is still pending despite repeated assurances over about two months.
Margin pressure: raw material costs up 2.8% from geopolitical issues plus event spending (SEMICON India, Transrail) compressed Q2 EBITDA margin slightly.
Plant throughput and bottleneck capacity now constrain delivery against the rising backlog.
SiC LOIs are non-binding; product qualification and reliability demonstration are still pending before sustained SiC revenue.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the financial run-rate and strategic positioning, but cautious and evasive on timelines and guidance: management repeatedly declined forward-looking revenue figures and pointed to Odisha government clearances as the open gating item.
key_quotes: So, from our side, almost everything is done. We are only doing internal testing of our reactors.
Now we have shifted our problem from market to the plant.
So, for 1B, we will not be having any more equity participation

adds.what: Odisha SiC epitaxy facility (clean room, 33 kV power, SiC epitaxial reactors installed; two reactors initially, may need about five)
Packaging (phase 1B) line funded by term loan with about 5% government interest subsidy, sanction pending

growth.why: No formal revenue guidance; management declined forward numbers but expects to beat current run-rate, backed by Rs 12-15 crore epitaxy revenue over four to six months, railways expected to grow 70-80% YoY, and Odisha SiC epi capacity awaiting state clearances (targeted Nov-Dec 2026), with HPD bottlenecks at ~90% utilisation.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin slipped to 16.6% from 17% a year earlier as raw material costs rose 2.8% and event spending weighed, and no cost action or mix benefit was guided; H1 margin did rise to 16.9% from 15.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Odisha SiC epitaxy clean room, 33 kV power and reactors are installed with only internal testing left; start awaits state building/fire clearances, hoped for Nov-Dec 2026, and HPD bottlenecks at ~90% are being doubled by adding machines.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Backlog about Rs 39 crore against a Rs 34 crore quarterly base, railways expected to grow 70-80% YoY, and epitaxy adds Rs 12-15 crore over four to six months, though HPD throughput at ~90% is the constraint.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: HPD bottleneck utilisation is ~90% and management says it is investing to increase capacity; packaging phase 1B term loan is approved pending sanction, and fabrication phase 2 is planned with no timeline.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management expects to do better than the current run-rate of about Rs 34 crore per quarter, backed by a Rs 39 crore backlog and railways expected to grow 70-80% YoY, but declined to give numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Odisha clearances have already slipped beyond earlier expectations with no firm date, and bank sanction for packaging has been pending for about two months, though management declined forward numbers so there is no formal guidance to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: SiC epitaxy wafers start commercial output once Odisha clearances land, with Rs 12-15 crore epi revenue expected over the next four to six months; first export order is about 70% executed and a BSV HVDC development plan is due within a month.

rows.label: Odisha statutory, building and fire clearances for SiC epi
rows.why: Management hopes for November or at latest December 2026, but no firm timeline has been given and the chairman's Q3 hope has already slipped.

rows.label: Railways and defence orders, plus US export testing
rows.why: Railways expected to grow 70-80% YoY in quantity and value this year with repeat orders; first export order is about 70% executed and first rail/defence orders are awaited.

rows.label: Packaging phase 1B term loan sanction (5% subsidy)
rows.why: Bank has internal approvals and the sanction letter is pending after about two months, and packaging takes 9-12 months to build once funded.

tone.note: Management was confident on the run-rate, backlog and railways, but cautious and declined forward revenue or EBITDA numbers; analysts pressed on the Odisha timeline, the $100 million figure and the epitaxy revenue estimate.
